proposition: On the pages read, the dissertation dates the first trial, in Herat before Shāhrukh, to c. 825/1422 (followed by a judgeship in Yazd), and a second summons to Herat, described as being tried again, to 829/1426 (with Nafsat al-Maṣdūr I and R. Iʿtiqādāt). The 830/1427 arrest, torture and exile after the attempt on Shāhrukh is narrated without the word trial on its own page, but chapter 3 says he 'twice stood trial and was exiled' between 828/1425 and 831/1428, which on a natural reading counts 1426 and 1427. The dissertation does not list the three trials by date in one place; that mapping is an inference from these pages.

mediation.who: Ibn Turka, Nafsat al-Maṣdūr I/II, as reported by Melvin-Koushki
